items.title: Show HN: NES Contra (1987) port (ASM –> C and then C –> WebAssembly)
items.author: tevlon
items.content:
I ported it in two steps. First to C: the game logic is translated routine by routine from the 6502 assembly, and checked frame by frame against the original in the Mesen emulator. Then the C code to WebAssembly so it runs in the browser.

The cherry on top: online multiplayer, so two players can play co-op over the internet.

items.title: Show HN: A language model that lives in a boot sector
items.author: kerlenton
items.content:
All the ideas came from the boot sector demo scene where people had been writing chess and BASIC games in 512 bytes, even a C compiler. I wondered what one can do using a neural network instead of a program and generating boot logs for non-existent hardware was something fun to try.

Entire inference engine is 510 bytes of MBR, weights, vocab, and strings reside in the sectors following MBR. Small char-level neural network was trained on dmesg generated by machine, so machine produces Linux boot messages infinitely.

train.py performs precisely the same integer arithmetic operations as the asm code does and thus produces an output identical character-by-character to the one produced by QEMU. The difference analysis revealed my favorite bug. The characters at the beginning matched those generated by the simulator, but then the output diverged. I retrieved the hidden layer via QEMU’s debug port and compared the neurons' values with those of the simulator, one neuron at a time. Only the value of the first neuron was correct. The activation involves idiv, and idiv stores its remainder in edx. The pointer to the biases table was stored in edx, which resulted in the first neuron being biased correctly and the following ones using garbage. Now the bias' address is determined from the loop counter, and no pointers have to survive the division. Another bug I found simply by looking at the code before I did my first run-through: the BIOS print routine zeros out bx, but bx contains the predicted character number. This explains the push and pop of bx surrounding the print.

sectorllm is the most similar to my project, as it runs an actual 5-layer llama2 with attention mechanism in just 1.2K of assembly code. It is the trade-off in the opposite direction, as my engine needs to fit into one sector and therefore my network has just one hidden layer of int8 operations for dreaming the dmesg.

items.title: Show HN: I rebuilt my old canvas 3D library as a small WebGL 2 library – phoria2
items.author: kevs3d
items.content:
is a small, fast JavaScript library for 3D on the web - charts, labelled scenes, dashboards and product viewers, on a WebGL 2 renderer with an API you can learn in an afternoon. Designed for ease-of-use by agents and humans from the ground up!

  • PBR materials, instancing, points, lines, labels, picking, shadows, particles and glTF models.
  • No runtime dependencies, plain ES modules, and views that only draw when something changes.
  • Every option is validated, a mistake comes back as an error that details the fix - for you, or your coding agent.
  • MIT licensed. , then find the code, the docs and a React example on GitHub.

A rewrite of , a JavaScript library from 2013 that rendered 3D onto the canvas 2D context. Back when we were still wizards.

items.title: Show HN: Arsaze – Cursor for video editing (Tab-complete and agent edits)
items.author: ArshadAzeezM
items.content: Everything a cut needs, by hand or by asking. Captions are transcribed with word timing and styled with reusable presets. Silences and filler words come out of a talking head in one pass, and Tab suggests your next edit as you work. Colour has wheels, curves, HSL secondaries, LUTs and shot matching. Audio has voice isolation, noise reduction, loudness and automatic ducking under speech. Images, video, voiceover, music and sound effects are generated straight onto the timeline. Export an MP4 with no watermark, or hand off to DaVinci Resolve and Premiere Pro as FCPXML. Arsaze also has background removal, motion tracking, Animate Studio motion graphics, an After Effects panel (beta), a free portfolio page and free in-browser tools. Every tool works by hand on the timeline, and every one is also a tool your AI can call.

items.title: Show HN: I Turned DOOM into a Transformer
items.author: falperc
items.content:
Instead of trying to run DOOM on things, I have instead decided to use DOOM (many, many, many doom games actually) to create a transformer. For a lot of the math required I essentially had to use DOOM game mechanics and voodoo dolls (DOOM is turing complete btw) and exchange them with the actual operations, essentially creating an alternative to NumPy (a 65000x slower one). Thus, I am proud to present DOOMFORMER. Here are a list of things DOOMFORMER can do :

It can classify MNIST digits, even if you write these digits on the map!

You can use it to make decisions, so, it can play DOOM. Yes! You can play DOOM with thousands of DOOM games now! The marine's mind can be controlled by DOOM, playing on a map generated by DOOMFORMER. Truly, the possibilities are endless, and even larger-scale training of DOOMFORMER could be done on a measly T4.

If anyone would like to help me scale this up and make crazier things, I'd love to work together.

items.title: Show HN: Auto Dismiss Mac OS "Allow <app> to find devices on local networks?"
items.author: johncassil
items.content: This popup has been a constant gripe of mine for years. I almost NEVER want to allow this permission and there is no system setting to disable it globally and prevent the popup from interrupting your typing, etc. This tiny swift app I built will autoclose it in 1/4th of a second and leave behind a little notification that it did so. Would love to hear feedback!

items.title: Show HN: Point your camera at a landscape to learn about its geology
items.author: headsupernova
items.content:
Geologic maps in augmented reality

Hold your phone up to a canyon wall, a road cut or a distant ridge, and the geologic map is drawn over the landscape. The rock in the center of the screen is identified, and nearby peaks and lakes are labeled. Select a rock to highlight it and gray out everything else.
